previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with recurrent primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for his 24th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy as part of reinduction therapy. He presented electively in stable condition and received methotrexate 8 g/m² with urinary alkalinization. Temozolomide 240 mg daily was restarted on the same day for a 7-day on/7-day off cycle. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately to 0.13, and he tolerated treatment without complications. Sodium remained stable, and no adjustments were needed to desmopressin. He was discharged home with instructions to continue leucovorin and bicarbonate for 24 hours, resume all home medications, and follow up in clinic for Rituxan and ongoing management.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
